data.exact_reserve_text: During 2017 we released prior year reserves of $176.9m (2016: $180.2m). Our specialty lines division increased reserve releases as the post recession portfolio from 2012 onwards matures. Specialty lines releases also included amounts from the 2014/2015 cyber portfolio, an area that has more variability than the rest of the specialty lines account. This counter-balanced lower releases on short tail classes where the mechanical effect of reduced margins on reserve releases, along with the effects of a large series of natural disasters, is now visable. data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported a net release of prior year reserves of $176.9m in 2017. Releases were driven primarily by favourable development in the specialty lines portfolio (including amounts from the 2014/2015 cyber portfolio and maturation of the post-recession 2012+ book). These releases were partially offset by lower releases on short-tail classes due to reduced margins and by significant 2017 natural catastrophe activity (Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, Mexican earthquakes and Californian wildfires) which increased current-year claims activity.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development figure (-176.9) taken from the Managing Agent's narrative 'During 2017 we released prior year reserves of $176.9m' and the division breakdown table. The report expresses amounts in US dollars and the reserve release is stated in $m; the narrative does not explicitly label the total as gross or net, however the division-level breakdown sums to the stated total which indicates a gross release presentation; confidence is high. Mappings of syndicate division names to the standard Lloyd's LOBs are best-fit where direct matches did not exist (e.g. 'Political, accident & contingency' mapped to 'Accident & Health' with low confidence). The claims development triangle is presented as percentages (gross) and has been captured from the Technical Provisions note.
